title: Federica Torgneur (Founder & CEO, Reveevo · ex-McKinsey · INSEAD MBA) — 'Someone had put into writing everything I had been thinking about building mission-driven businesses'
summary: Torgneur founded Reveevo and runs it as CEO; she worked at McKinsey and holds an INSEAD MBA. She found the book through a webinar hosted by PURPOSE® while researching the legal and governance structures open to mission-driven founders, then completed the six-week Early Stage Founders Cohort built around it and led by Marny Sumrall. Her recap lists what the group worked through: each company's mission, its fiduciary ranking, embedding the mission across an organisation, the mission-related failures to expect, and the legal protections available.
blockquote:
Last week I wrapped up an inspirational six weeks of the Incorruptible Early Stage Founders Cohort.
 
In the past months, I have been deep into researching legal and governance frameworks for founders building mission-driven businesses. Thanks to a webinar hosted by PURPOSE®, I learned about Eric Ries's new book, Incorruptible, which turned out to be one of the best books I read recently (can't recommend it enough!). Most of all, I finally felt like someone had put into writing everything I had been thinking about building mission-driven businesses that do more than maximizing shareholder value.
 
For those who haven't read Incorruptible yet, Eric argues that companies drift from their mission because of "financial gravity," the structural pull of investor expectations and short-term incentives that erodes even well intentioned organizations as they succeed, with the results, at times, to damage (if not even kill) the company itself. His answer is to build protection in early through mission-locked governance, before success makes the mission a target worth stripping away.
